We need to determine appropriate crime(s) based on facts. The scenario: In prison, a prisoner (王X) gets into a quarrel with another inmate, picks up an empty glass bottle, tries to hit the other inmate, police intervene, push him, he collides with a police officer (段XX) and then, not obeying police, he uses the glass bottle to hit the officer's head, causing scalp laceration. So assault on a police officer (public security personnel) with a dangerous weapon (glass bottle) causing injury. Likely crime: "故意伤害罪" (intentional injury) and "妨害公务罪" (obstructing public duty) maybe also "非法持有、私藏枪支" not relevant. The examples show for similar case: In earlier example with a driver biting police, they gave "危险驾驶;妨害公务". That case involved assault on police (biting) and dangerous driving. Here we have assault on police, causing injury. The appropriate charge: "故意伤害罪" (intentional injury) and "妨害公务罪" (obstructing official duties). In Chinese criminal law, assault on police while they are performing duties can be charged as "妨害公务罪". If injury is caused, also "故意伤害罪". In examples, they sometimes combine both: e.g., earlier example with "强制猥亵、侮辱妇女" they combined. For assault on police, they used "妨害公务". In the example with dangerous driving and "妨害公务", they combined both. So we likely need both: "故意伤害;妨害公务". Check if any other crime like "聚众扰乱公共场所秩序" not relevant. So answer: [罪名]故意伤害;妨害公务<eoa>
